title: Freedom of Speech Legislation Amendment (Censorship) Bill 2018
short_title: Freedom of Speech Legislation Amendment (Censorship) Bill 2018

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would remove or narrow several restrictions on publications, films, games, subscription television and online content, and repeal the election advertising blackout.
It would allow specified adult material through restricted access systems and remove morality-based refusal criteria, while retaining restrictions on child sexual material and criminal instruction.
Most provisions would begin the day after Royal Assent, with National Classification Code amendments taking effect six months later to allow state and territory consideration.
changes: The separate requirement to refuse classification to material advocating terrorism would be repealed.
Area-specific prohibitions on certain material in the Northern Territory and associated seizure powers would be removed.
The Classification Board would retain discretion over advertisements, with narrower grounds requiring refusal.
Guidance about community suitability standards in datacasting codes would be limited to services without access controls.
summary.affected: Subscription television broadcasters, online content services, datacasting licensees, the Classification Board and people in designated Northern Territory areas would be affected.
